questions.question: What is DIAL?
questions.answer: DIAL stands for Deterministic Integrator of Applications and is an open-source AI framework with an API-first approach for building custom applications to tackle complex problems using LLMs.

questions.question: What is the DIAL Marketplace?
questions.answer: The DIAL Marketplace is a centralized hub of all accessible models, applications, and assistants within the DIAL enterprise ecosystem.

questions.question: What programming framework is used to develop DIAL applications?
questions.answer: DIAL applications are developed using LangChain along with the DIAL SDK and deployment package.

relevant_context.transcript_id: DIAL for Developers: Part 2 - Developing Your First DIAL Application

questions.question: How can DIAL be integrated with Microsoft Copilot Studio?
questions.answer: DIAL applications can be called from Microsoft Copilot Studio while preserving conversation context.

relevant_context.transcript_id: DIAL Integrations: Part 1 - Calling DIAL Applications from Microsoft Copilot Studio

questions.question: What are DIAL Quick Apps?
questions.answer: DIAL Quick Apps are low-code applications built with DIAL's application server and Marketplace features, allowing users to quickly create apps for specific tasks.

questions.question: How can DIAL be deployed from Google Cloud Marketplace?
questions.answer: DIAL can be deployed from the Google Cloud Marketplace and users can sign in to explore all DIAL features.

relevant_context.transcript_id: DIAL Deployment from Google Cloud Marketplace
